When disaster strikes, communication can fail exactly when people need it most.
Sethu is designed to help emergency reports travel between nearby devices using local Bluetooth communication, without relying on cloud services for its intended offline workflow.
The Sender sends an SOS to a nearby Relay. The Relay stores the report locally and confirms receipt.
Even when the original connection disappears, the stored report remains available for onward delivery.
When the Coordinator becomes available, the user establishes the next connection. Sethu then forwards the pending report automatically, and records delivery after the required acknowledgement.
Behind the interface are local storage, controlled message delivery, acknowledgement handling, and an offline-first architecture designed for resilience.
Sethu. When connectivity breaks, emergency communication should still have a path.
